newsitem.title: UK: Mark pressured on crosses as stg, dlr race ahead.
newsitem.headline: Mark pressured on crosses as stg, dlr race ahead.

text.p: The mark was under downward pressure on its crosses at European midsession as the dollar and sterling steamed ahead to hit new multiple-year highs.
Dollar/mark surged to its strongest in almost six years to eye the key 1.80 marks point, while sterling/mark climbed to its highest level since October 1990 at 3.0150.

"There doesn't seem to be any special driving force. The market's got the bit between its teeth and is driving sterling higher, dragging the dollar up with it, and the mark is falling," said Keith Edmonds, chief analyst at IBJ in London.
The French franc bucked the trend, losing ground against the mark, but dealers noted that volume was thin as French markets were closed for Bastille Day.
The mark was trading at 3.3813/16 French francs at 1047 GMT compared to late Friday's level here of 3.3764/69. Mark/Paris was helped by dollar/French franc's push to its strongest since August 1993.

Meantime, the market bubbled with talk of Bank of France intervention on Irish punt/franc to keep the 15 percent ERM bands intact. The punt -- the strongest unit in the EMS grid -- was trading nearly 13 percent above the weakest-placed franc.
The punt firmed to 2.6994/44 marks from 2.6869/19 late Friday.

Traders said options activity in dollar/Paris had fed through into mark/Paris. The U.S. unit's rise through 6.00 francs had triggered options knockouts, and that effect had been magnified by holiday-thinned turnover, they said.
